```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4)
```

The `BR_*()` functions accept a `SingleCellExperiment` as well as a
Seurat object, and give the same text. The plots are drawn with scater
instead of Seurat. The differences to know:

- Groups come from `colLabels()` (the `label` column of `colData`)
  unless you pass `group.by`. Seurat's equivalent is the active identity.
- `BR_ElbowPlot()` needs the `varExplained` attribute that
  `scater::runPCA()` stores on the PCA.
- `BR_FeaturePlot()` describes the `logcounts` assay by default
  (`layer = "counts"` to change it).

## A small dataset

We build an SCE from the counts of `pbmc_small` and run a standard
scater workflow. As labels we reuse the clusters that came with the
data.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(scBrailleR)
library(scater)
data("pbmc_small", package = "SeuratObject")

sce <- SingleCellExperiment(
  assays = list(counts = SeuratObject::LayerData(pbmc_small, layer = "counts"))
)
sce <- logNormCounts(sce)
set.seed(1)
sce <- runPCA(sce, ncomponents = 15)
sce <- runTSNE(sce, dimred = "PCA", perplexity = 10)
colLabels(sce) <- pbmc_small$RNA_snn_res.1
sce
```

## Elbow, clusters, genes

```{r elbow}
BrailleR::VI(BR_ElbowPlot(sce))
```

```{r dimplot}
BrailleR::VI(BR_DimPlot(sce, reduction = "TSNE"))
```

```{r featureplot}
BrailleR::VI(BR_FeaturePlot(sce, c("CD3E", "LYZ"), reduction = "TSNE"))
```

See `vignette("seurat", package = "scBrailleR")` for how to read each
part of the output; the meaning is identical.

## Without labels

If the SCE has no `label` column, `BR_FeaturePlot()` still describes
where each gene is expressed but cannot say which group that is, and
`BR_DimPlot()` asks for `group.by`:

```{r nolabels, error = TRUE}
sce$label <- NULL
BrailleR::VI(BR_FeaturePlot(sce, "LYZ", reduction = "TSNE"))
BR_DimPlot(sce)
```
